VOLTAGE ACROSS L1 - CH1 monitors voltage at the top of L1. CH2 monitors voltage at the bottom of L1. Adding CH1 to an inverted CH2, produces a voltage signal that equals the voltage drop of L1.
Remember, in a series circuit current is the same at all points. Current and voltage are in phase across a resistor...
On most oscilloscopes current can not be measured directly. Measuring the voltage across a resistor with an oscilloscope can be used to indicate the phase and value of current.

MEASURING CURRENT - Some oscilloscopes have a special current probe. These are expensive and are not normally available to the technician for troubleshooting. It is useful to know how to measure current using the voltage drop across a resistor.

The voltage across inductors are in phase with each other (but not in phase with the voltage across a resistor) and can be added directly.
Also notice that as XL increases the circuit becomes more inductive. The voltage across the inductor increases and the voltage across the resistor decreases.
Now lets observe the overall phase relationship between R and XL in a series circuit.
The phase relationship can be shown by measuring the voltages across R and L using an oscilloscope. Remember, once the trigger level has been established do not change it.
